name: Rover Site 8 (Sols 239-278): sample-depot dwell location
description: Documented Perseverance rover position (RMC Site 8) where the rover remained stationary from sol 239 through sol 278 while CACHECAM imaged a sample-tube caching activity (558 CACHECAM frames recorded in this window). This is the rover's own localized stop, not a georeferenced rock or outcrop target: it establishes where the rover was during the caching campaign, not the precise position of any individual cached tube or depot marker.

provenance_detail.product: best_interp.csv / best_tactical.csv (Mars2020 Rover PLACES, data localization bundle)
provenance_detail.cross_check: best_tactical.csv ROVER record site=7 drive=2440 sol=239 (sclk 688162709) immediately precedes this SITE row; observations.csv shows CACHECAM frames beginning at sclk 690224439.974, inside the sol 239-278 dwell before the next drive (site=8 drive=64, sol 278).
provenance_detail.coordinate_reference_frame: Site-frame rover localization reported in planetocentric latitude/longitude and in Jezero_Crater_Projection northing/easting (same equidistant-cylindrical convention, standard parallel 18.4663N, as this project's DEM/zone CRS); verified consistent across best_interp.csv and best_tactical.csv.

dem_validation.checked_via: backend/app/data.py point_sample() against the project's resampled CTX DEM/slope/cost rasters

limitations: Rover localization proves where the rover stood, not the exact position of a specific cached sample tube or rock target.
No independent georeferenced science-target product (e.g. an abrasion-patch or sample-tube coordinate list) was available locally to refine this beyond the rover's own position.

Horizontal uncertainty of the PLACES localization itself is not restated here; see the Mars2020_Rover_PLACES_PDS_SIS.pdf product documentation bundled with the source data for the stated per-product accuracy.
